content.text:
Analyse the training examples:
In each example, there is a background of 9 (maroon) and several connected components of 1 (blue).
Some components of 1 are changed to 8 (teal), while others remain 1.

Let's check the property of the components turned into 8 vs remaining 1:
Example 1:
Two components of 1:
1) rows 1-4, cols 5-7. Bounding box: 4x3. Contains a loop/hole?
At row 1: [1,1,1]
row 2: [.,.,1]
row 3: [1,.,1]
row 4: [1,1,1]
Does it enclose something? (3,6) is 9, but (2,5), (2,6) are 9, so it has an opening at (2,5),(2,6)?
Wait, row 1 cols 5,6,7: 1,1,1
row 2 col 7: 1
row 3 cols 5,7: 1,1
row 4 cols 5,6,7: 1,1,1
So at (2,5), (2,6) it's 9. It's not a closed loop.
Second component:
row 7: cols 5..10 (6 pixels)
row 8: cols 6, 10
row 9: cols 6, 10
row 10: cols 6, 10
row 11: cols 6..10
row 12: col 10
Has a closed loop! Between rows 7 and 11, cols 6 and 10:
row 7 has 5..10, row 11 has 6..10.
Enclosed region: (8,7..9), (9,7..9), (10,7..9) - 9 pixels enclosed!
The one turned to 8 has an enclosed loop?
Wait! In Example 1, the bottom component is turned to 8. It encloses an interior (hole).

Example 2:
Component 1 (top):
row 0: 7,8,9,10
row 1: 8,10
row 2: 8
row 3: 8,10
row 4: 8,9,10,11
Notice (2,9) is 9, (2,10) is 9. It doesn't close a loop.
Component 2 (bottom):
row 8: 6,7,8,9
row 9: 6,9
row 10: 6,7,8,9,10
Does it enclose (9,7) and (9,8)?
Row 8: 6,7,8,9 are 1.
Row 9: 6 is 1, 7 is 9, 8 is 9, 9 is 1.
Row 10: 6,7,8,9 are 1.
Yes! (9,7) and (9,8) are completely surrounded by 1s (4-connected or 8-connected)!
And Component 2 turned into 8!

Example 3:
Component 1 (top-left):
rows 0-4, cols 0-4.
row 0: 1 1 1 1 1
row 1: 1 . . 1 .
row 2: 1 . . 1 .
row 3: 1 . . 1 .
row 4: 1 1 1 1 1
This is a closed box! Encloses (1..3, 1..2).
It turned to 8!
Component 2 (top-mid):
row 0: 7,8,9
row 1: 9
row 2: 7,8,9
Open on left. Remained 1.
Component 3 (top-right):
row 0: 12,13,14,15
row 1: 12,15
row 2: 12,14,15 (at 13 it's 9, but row 3 has nothing). Open. Remained 1.
Component 4 (bottom-mid):
row 5: 6,7,8
row 6: 8
row 7: 6,8
row 8: 6,8
row 9: 6,7,8,9
Open at row 6. Remained 1.
Component 5 (bottom-right):
row 5: 12,13,14
row 6: 12,14
row 7: 12,14
row 8: 12,14
row 9: 12,13,14,15
Encloses (6..8, 13)!
Turned to 8!

Example 4:
Component 1 (top):
row 3: 1,2,3,4,5
row 4: 2,4
row 5: 2,4
Remained 1.
Component 2 (bottom-left):
row 8: 3,4,5,6
row 9: 3,6
row 10: 3,4,5,6
Encloses (9,4), (9,5). Turned to 8!
Component 3 (bottom-right):
row 7: 13
row 8: 9,10,11,12,13
row 9: 9,13
row 10: 9,13
row 11: 9,13
row 12: 9,10,11,12,13
Encloses (9..11, 10..12)! Turned to 8!

Conclusion:
Any component of 1 that encloses at least one cell (a hole of 9s, 4-connected topology where background cannot reach the edge of the grid without crossing 1s, or 8-connected loop) is recolored to 8.
Specifically, background cells (9) that are not connected to the border of the grid: any component of 1 that encloses such cells is recolored to 8.

I am ready for the test input.An observation across all examples is that any blue (1) connected component that encloses a hole (i.e. contains interior background cells that cannot reach the edge of the grid) is recolored to teal (8). Blue shapes without an enclosed hole remain blue (1).

Please provide the test input grid.
